owner_copy.text: Pause, take a deep breath & exhale. You are home.
Perched on the edge of a picture perfect white sandy beach, The Sandhya, with its unassuming minimalist architecture and its luxurious contemporary aesthetics is calling you home.

Designed to feel like an exclusive private beach house with the amenities of an intimate boutique hotel, your relaxation starts as you kick off your shoes and slip through the hidden door in the wide wooden façade.

Inside , you will catch the first glimpses of our star attraction, The Indian Ocean, magnificent and omnipresent in every part of the hotel including all our Studios and Suite. With panoramic glass doors & windows though out, this captivating view is our artwork.

The Indian Ocean is your constant companion at The Sandhya. Whether you are enjoying the sunshine on the expansive lawns, lounging all day around our abundant, airy indoor living spaces or cooling off in our air-conditioned media room, the sea is always your view. Savour internationally-inspired snacks, meals and cocktails at The Dining Room then retreat to one of our spacious 9 bedrooms, never losing the view of the turquoise waters.
Dipping your feet in the azure waters of our brand new 30-meter swimming pool, you will soon be hypnotised by the allure of the white tipped surf breaks just a few meters ahead.

Designed with luxury and comfort in mind, our property’s furnishings are inspired by mid-century aesthetics and embellished with mod-chinoiserie decor. Our Singaporean owner’s discerning vision has been brought to life by the local designers and craftsmen he worked with across Sri Lanka.

Come evening, as temperature cools and the sun begins to set over the majestic Indian Ocean, the beauty of twilight is undeniable with its ethereal glow of orange, pink and blue hues painting the cotton candy-clouded sky.

Our 9 spacious rooms are the epitome of quiet elegance, design excellence, thoughtful detail and home comforts. All our retreat rooms have unobstructed sweeping views of the white sandy beach and beyond to the endless ocean, each with its own private balcony or exclusive patio area. We have included thoughtful touches from evening lavender scents to high pressure rain showers so you are assured of a restorative stay in any one of our room types – Studio King/Twin (38 sq m), Studio+ King (43 sq m) and Director’s Suite (76 sq m).

Elevated Comfort Food using the freshest of locally-sourced ingredients was the brief for our menu designers and chefs. Working closely with our owner, a self-confessed “easy foodie”, the team conjured a delectable array of dishes inspired from a global set-list of food heaven highlights. If you don’t find what you crave, simply ask our team to prepare what your tummy desires. Dishes catering to vegetarian, vegan, keto and other dietary lifestyles are available.

From our signature Sri Lankan rice & curry, our zesty DIY poke bowls, our localized “Tom Yum” style noodles with fresh Ceylon prawns or going directly to a finger licking array of delicious homemade desserts, we truly believe some of the island‘s best qualities may be expressed through our food, exploring the diversity of the local produce available.
Our breads, pastas, sauces, infused mayonnaise, stocks, spice blends, jams are made in-house and the menus subtly evolve with the seasons but rest assured, the quality remains.

Elevated Comfort Food was the brief for our visiting menu designer, Chef Christophe DuBois. Working closely with our owner, a self-confessed “easy foodie”, the team conjured a delectable array of dishes inspired from a global set-list of food heaven highlights.

Casual Luxe is at the heart of our ethos at The Sandhya. We prioritise understated design, thoughtful form and practical function above conspicuous bling and glitter. Blending timeless mid-century modern design with the natural elements around us is an art form that we continually practice. Simple luxury resonates through clean lines and symmetry, allowing for the beauty of our surroundings to shine.

Calming and contemporary yet indulgent and spacious rooms for hiding away in private and convivial-feel common areas for communally sharing with other guests define what the discerning and sophisticated traveler craves.
Our service is warm, kind, attentive yet informal. Ask for your heart’s desire or simply be left alone when seeking that self-restoration. Just feel at home and allow us to look after you.

We support the vibrant local community and our stunning environment. From a zero-food waste menu, a ban on single-use plastic, water recycling, a care programme for our beach turtles through to protecting our shoreline by using an up-cycled shipping container for our unique swimming pool, we strive for sustainable tourism and a lifelong family member to Mother Nature.
We have blended the best of the worlds that we live in. We are not international. We are not local. We are simply The Sandhya.

Imagine the perfect holiday destination. A mile long, white sandy beach, swaying palm trees, a front row seat to magical sunsets, world renowned sites and a plethora of activities close-by yet guaranteed relaxation even closer. This is exactly what The Sandhya offers.

Kabalana Beach, on the golden south coast of Sri Lanka just by the buzzing and eclectic town of Ahangama has come into its own in recent years with surfers, families, and digital nomads alike. Pristine sand, stunning sunsets and a consistent swell has nurtured a laid-back scene where surf lovers, beach bunnies, serial retreat hunters and quiet couples coexist with welcoming locals.

Beyond the boundaries of The Sandhya and Kabalana Beach lies a guidebook full of interesting day activities, shopping expedition, gourmet experiences or tranquil exploration of the coastal belt or the impossibly green interior.

Centuries old Galle Fort, the crowning jewel of southern Sri Lanka and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is just 25 minutes away. While away a whole day browsing through an eclectic array of boutiques, stopping for well-earned sips and bites from an ever-growing cafe and restaurant scene. Start your historical exploration with a breezy walk around the perimeter of the fort atop the fortified rampart walls, take in the iconic white lighthouse, and pause to watch local kids leap from Flag Rock into the deep azure waters below. The winding backstreets of Galle Fort are a haven for shopaholics, dotted with boutiques selling colourful clothing, beautiful homewares and memorable souvenirs.

Discover amazing surf points, whale-watching boat rides and a dizzying array of dining options at the nearby beaches of Midigama, Weligama, Mirissa, Madiha and Hiriketiya Bay. Our own town Ahangama has grown into a foodies’ haven with a diverse selection of high-quality eateries and night spots all within a stone’s throw from us.

World famous Yala and Udwalawe National Parks, Singharaja Forest and awe-inspiring waterfalls are within manageable day trips from The Sandhya. Depart your room in the crisp early morning and be back in time for a late lunch or cocktail while taking in the stunning sunset right on our very own Kabalana Beach.

Our home at The Sandhya can be your very own private beach house with an Exclusive Use booking. Our prime location on Kabalana Beach with its unique position nestled in a secluded nook lends itself to an intimate wedding party, birthday celebration, family reunion, wellness/fitness retreat or simply to celebrate life. With the sunset as our daily back drop, the beach as your blank canvas and with our delightful staff at your service, we offer the perfect private setting for your special occasion.

quotes.text: We were very pleased with our stay at this hotel. The location is very convenient: Weligama and Galle are a 20-30-minute drive away, where there are plenty of well-rated restaurants and cafes. Two souvenir shops are a five-minute walk away. The hotel is clean. All the photos are accurate. The rooms are cleaned twice, and they always make sure there's drinking water in the room. There's a good restaurant on-site for lunch and dinner if you don't feel like driving anywhere. And a bonus is the opportunity to see the sunset. For surfers, there are various surfing schools within a minute's walk. For me, the hotel's biggest advantage was its small size, so there's no hustle and bustle. There's also no street noise: although the hotel is located along the road, all the rooms face the ocean, so you can't hear the road at all (only the ocean).

quotes.text: Beautiful property on great stretch of Kabalana beach. It was really nice walking along the long stretch of beach and having a dip in the warm and clear water. The king size bedroom was big, clean and very comfortable. The pool area was relaxing with comfortable sun beds with a great view of the beach and also direct access. We enjoyed eating lunch at the pool area with some of the best king prawns we had, deep fried in panko breadcrumbs. Everything we had for lunch and breakfast was good quality and value. There is also a fantastic restaurant just opposite if you want a change. The personnel were all brilliant, helping whenever they had to, and replenishing cold water bottles when we on our sun beds. We had 2 lovely and memorable nights and would not hesitate to return.

We ate by pool twice and both times food was excellent Pool Area Kept spotless at all times , the crashing of the waves is all you here Plenty of sun beds and pool is huge in comparison to hotel size Staff Staff are very helpful and friendly, from the guy at the security gate to all inside staff - A big thank you , thanks to Dhillan for making breakfast and our birthdays great Overall A fantastic hotel which felt like being in a big house rather than hotel, very personal and highly recommend

quotes.note: Names a staff member by first name (Dhillan).

quotes.text: A great stay, absolutely gorgeous hotel - perfect, friendly and attentive service, small hotel so felt very safe, familiar and luxurious. Delicious food, excellent location to get to Ahangama by 5min TukTuk and be directly on a wide sandy and long (enough) beach with lots of surfers, without the actual beach being packed full of people so was calm but bustling. Would highly recommend.
quotes.author: Guest User

quotes.text: Minimalist design, open and light central atrium. There's a laid back vibe from arrival, with welcoming retro lounge furniture, unfortunately the choice to not provide air conditioning to this area makes it unbearably hot for almost the entire day/night, only when storms rolled in did people sit enjoying the space. We opted for the larger room with pool access, I don't think it's necessary the standard pool access rooms looked more than adequate. The room is very large with a decent size and very comfortable bed. The bathroom has separate bath and shower with twin sinks, in the room is a good sized safe that accomdates a large SLR camera easily, there are bath robes and single use slippers. There are also multi country plug sockets. There is no fridge and no kettle, but you can make use of the kitchenette. The house keeping was good but turn down service was hit or miss. For the most part noise from the road isn't disturbing when around by the pool, the sound of waves crashing is the constant soundtrack. Although the pool area is limited to guests only, we did notice on some days more people than rooms. The breakfast is very nice, although the outdoor tables are too small for the plates and dishes. There is a small kitchen area to help yourself for tea /coffee with wine/lion beer (at a cost). This seems like a nice idea but execution feels jumbled. If you need to find a staff member as the hotel often feels deserted, open the fridge, one will appear. The view from the property across the beach is wonderful, although it's clear there is a battle happening, illegal structures built on the beach were destroyed by police, much of the debris remained on the beach for days, the hotel has made efforts to tidy up but more structures have arrived, sadly this is symptomatic of a wider problem of lack of pride in a beautiful country with no thought to dumping garbage anywhere and everywhere Overall the hotel is very nice, kept to a high standard but after spending 4weeks touring SL, this hotel feels very expensive for the amenities and at times the service didn't have the warmth we experienced elsewhere, my 4 rating is generous as I feel 3 is too harsh.
quotes.author: Guest User
quotes.note: Mixed: praises the view and rooms, criticises lounge heat, service warmth and price. Recorded so the picture is not cherry-picked. Over the 600-character testimonial limit; never trim it.

quotes.text: The hotel got the dates of our trip wrong, and didn’t send confirmation. They then messaged late the day before our arrival to ask what time we were arriving. To which I replied 11:00. They then refused to let me change the date, or offer a refund. Both of which they then said they would offer and then threatened me with the police. I was then left with insufficient funds to book alternative accommodation and they still took the money despite their error. They then sent me numerous emails to try and say that I had received my booking confirmation. Just don’t waste your time booking with them.
quotes.author: Guest User
quotes.note: Negative: a booking dispute. Recorded so the picture is not cherry-picked; not for the site.

press.quote: Standing out from the traditional guesthouses and villas on Sri Lanka’s idyllic Kabalana Beach, the Sandhya is a modern boutique hotel that’s sleek but understated.

press.quote: A departure from the typical colonial- style villas or local surf shack properties that line Sri Lanka’s south coast to the east of Galle, The Sandhya is a head- turner. Set on a powdery white sands of Kabalana Beach, steps away from the turquoise surf, the low-slung property’s clean, sharp lines serve as a contemporary canvas for a mood board imbued with Scandinavian sensibilities.

No nightly price anywhere: the only price on the site is the US$3,500++ exclusive use. A visitor must reach the engine to learn a rate.

No reviews or ratings anywhere on the site, though the listings score 9.3 to 9.7 out of 10. No check-in or check-out times, and breakfast is never mentioned although the engine lists it as complimentary.

Booking panel: tapped with its default dates kept, it opened the engine with empty dates (#checkin=&checkout=) although it displays today and tomorrow. With dates picked it was not tested; the calendar would not respond to the automated tap. Dates shown are DD/MM/YYYY. The cookie notice sits inside the panel.

WhatsApp icon beside the phone number, but the link is tel:. There is no wa.me link.
